issues.visual_id: Revenue Trend and Gross Margin % Trend
issues.observed: Months are displayed in a non-chronological sequence such as April, August, December, February, January and July. This makes both trend lines analytically misleading.
issues.desired: Months should follow fiscal or calendar chronology consistently, with the chosen fiscal sequence made clear.
issues.action: Create or use a numeric MonthSort/FiscalMonthNumber column, set MonthName to Sort by Column, and validate the sequence for every fiscal year before publishing.

issues.observed: TotalRevenue and YoYGrowthPct appear to share one value axis. Revenue columns reach approximately £1.6M while the percentage series is compressed against zero and cannot be interpreted.
issues.desired: Revenue should be shown as columns and YoY growth as a clearly readable line or marker series on a percentage secondary axis.
issues.action: Use Power BI's line and clustered column chart with TotalRevenue on the primary currency axis and YoYGrowthPct on the secondary percentage axis. Add concise labels and conditionally colour negative growth.

issues.observed: The horizontal category chart combines revenue and growth on one numeric scale, leaving the YoY growth series effectively invisible as a thin red mark at zero.
issues.desired: Executives should be able to compare category revenue and growth without incompatible units suppressing one measure.
issues.action: Prefer a revenue bar chart with YoY growth shown through aligned labels or markers on a separate percentage scale. If the standard horizontal visual cannot support this cleanly, use two aligned visuals with synchronized category sorting rather than plotting both units on one axis.

issues.observed: The four large values have no visible business labels, so viewers must infer which number represents revenue, gross margin, YoY growth and risk areas.
issues.desired: Each card should have a concise label, clearly formatted value, semantic status and relevant comparison context.
issues.action: Add visible titles above the values: Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth and Risk Areas. Include prior-period variance or target context where supported, and use red status treatment for elevated risk rather than relying on position alone.

issues.observed: The third KPI displays 109.6%, which may represent either growth or an index/current-to-prior ratio. With no label or comparison context, its meaning is ambiguous and could be misread as 109.6% growth.
issues.desired: The displayed value must match the documented YoYGrowthPct measure semantics and be unambiguous to executives.
issues.action: Validate the DAX definition without changing its intended semantics. If the measure is a ratio of 1.096, label it as an index or create a separately governed growth measure returning 9.6%. If it genuinely represents 109.6% growth, retain it and add prior-year context.

issues.observed: A prominent grey trial-capacity banner spans the top of the deployed dashboard.
issues.desired: The executive-facing production page should be free from trial, licensing and development notices.
issues.action: Deploy the report through appropriately licensed production capacity or a supported distribution method that removes the trial banner. This is a tenant/capacity configuration issue rather than a report theme change.

issues.observed: No visible date, region or category controls are provided on the page, and there is no reset-filter affordance or visible filter-state summary.
issues.desired: A compact control row should expose the main executive slicing dimensions while preserving chart space and making active filters obvious.
issues.action: Add synchronized Date/Fiscal Period, Region and Category slicers in a single top row, plus a reset-bookmark button. Show the selected period in the page subtitle and avoid hiding all relevant state solely in the filter pane.

issues.observed: Titles and legends expose technical field names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarginPct, MonthName, FiscalYear and YoYGrowthPct.
issues.desired: Board-facing labels should use natural business language and concise titles.
issues.action: Rename labels for this visual to Total Revenue, Gross Margin %, Month, Fiscal Year and YoY Growth. Shorten titles to Revenue Trend, Gross Margin % Trend, Regional Performance and Category Performance.

issues.observed: The trend charts compare 2022 and 2023 as separate lines, but the page provides no current-period framing, latest-month annotation or explanation of whether these are fiscal years.
issues.desired: The page should immediately establish the reporting period and make current versus prior performance easy to understand.
issues.action: Add an 'As of' or selected fiscal-period subtitle. Keep the two-year comparison only if it supports the governed analysis; otherwise use a single chronological current-period series with prior-year comparison in tooltip or a clearly distinguished secondary line.

issues.observed: Green is used for revenue while red represents the entire YoY series, regardless of whether growth is positive or negative. The same red/green pair also represents fiscal years, producing conflicting meanings.
issues.desired: Neutral brand colours should identify measures or periods, while red and green should be reserved for negative and positive status.
issues.action: Use a consistent primary blue or other neutral brand colour for revenue, a secondary neutral colour for comparison years, and conditional red/green only for negative/positive growth or risk status. Check contrast for colour-vision accessibility.

issues.observed: The value 14 has no label, severity cue, trend, threshold or drill path explaining what constitutes a risk area.
issues.desired: RiskCount should communicate whether the count is improving or worsening and enable executives to reach the underlying risks.
issues.action: Label the card Risk Areas, apply threshold-based status colour backed by governed business rules, show change versus the prior period, and configure drillthrough or a tooltip to summarize the highest-impact risks.

issues.observed: Categories are not ordered by descending revenue, reducing scan efficiency and obscuring rank.
issues.desired: The strongest and weakest categories should be immediately apparent.
issues.action: Sort categories descending by TotalRevenue unless a governed business order is required. Retain consistent category order across related pages.

issues.observed: There is no page title, reporting-period subtitle or clear separation between KPI cards and analytical sections. Large numbers float above the visuals without containers.
issues.desired: The page should present a clear title and period, a coherent KPI band, then trend and driver sections.
issues.action: Add an Executive Overview heading and selected-period subtitle. Place KPIs in equal-width card containers, align chart edges to a consistent grid, and use subtle section spacing rather than heavy decoration.

issues.observed: Month labels are angled and one label is truncated as 'Septem...'. Axis and legend text is small relative to the available canvas.
issues.desired: Labels should remain readable at normal executive viewing distance without truncation.
issues.action: After correcting month order, use short month labels such as Apr, May and Jun, increase axis text size, and provide enough plot width. Avoid diagonal labels where a compact horizontal abbreviation will fit.

issues.observed: Only two regions are displayed across a wide plotting area, leaving substantial unused space.
issues.desired: The visual should use its allocated space efficiently while accurately reflecting the available data.
issues.action: Do not fabricate additional regions. If two regions are the complete filtered result, reduce the visual width or use compact ranked bars with labels; if filters are active, expose that state clearly.

summary: The actual page contains the required KPI and performance topics, but it is not yet board-ready. The most serious analytical defect is the non-chronological month ordering, followed by regional and category visuals that plot currency and percentage measures on the same scale, making growth unreadable. Missing KPI labels, absent page filters, technical field names, conflicting colour semantics and the production trial banner further weaken executive credibility. Most report-level deficiencies are readily fixable with standard Power BI formatting, sorting, combo-chart and layout capabilities; measure semantics should be validated rather than changed merely to resemble the reference.
reference_rejected_ideas: The reference's full application shell, left navigation rail and top Power BI-style command bar are not necessary analytical content and may be controlled by the embedding host rather than the report canvas.
Exact replication of the reference's miniature KPI sparklines is optional because they are not part of the specified required visuals and can add noise without a clearly governed time grain.

The reference's category revenue bars with separately positioned growth dots and a dashed divider may require layered visuals or a custom visual; a clean pair of aligned native visuals is more maintainable if equivalent interaction cannot be achieved accessibly.
The reference should not be copied if its illustrative values, region set, category set or date range differ from the deployed semantic model.
Red and green status styling from the reference should only be used when backed by defined thresholds and should not replace accessible labels or symbols.
